name: Four Seasons Hualalai
insider_take: Nestled along the pristine Kohala Coast of Hawaii's Big Island, Four Seasons Hualalai is not just a resort — it's a living, breathing piece of paradise built around an ancient lava field, where manta rays glide nightly beneath the surface of a natural lava-rock pool.
whats_special: Four Seasons Hualalai sits at the base of the dormant Hualalai volcano, offering an unmatched blend of raw Hawaiian nature and world-class luxury. The resort's crown jewel, the King's Pond — a 1.8-million-gallon natural lava-rock snorkel pool filled with tropical fish and sea turtles — is entirely unique in the world. Bungalow-style accommodations are scattered among swaying palms and lava gardens, giving the property an intimate, almost private-island feel. The resort also boasts a Jack Nicklaus-designed championship golf course that winds dramatically through ancient lava fields.
pro_tip: Book the Manta Ray Night Snorkel experience — every evening, bright lights attract plankton to the waters just off shore, drawing majestic manta rays in a breathtaking natural spectacle available only steps from the resort. Reserve your spot early as it fills up fast!
dont_miss: Don't miss a visit to the resort's Cultural Center , where ancient Hawaiian petroglyphs are preserved directly on the property's lava fields — a rare and humbling reminder that this sacred land has been cherished for centuries. Also, time a sunset dinner at Beach Tree , the resort's open-air oceanfront restaurant, for a meal and a view you'll never forget.
pros: Pristine oceanfront location on exclusive Kona-Kohala Coast
Championship Jack Nicklaus-designed golf course on property
Multiple award-winning restaurants and world-class spa facilities
Spacious suites and villas with private lanais and ocean views
cons: Premium luxury pricing reflects exclusive resort status
Remote Big Island location requires inter-island travel from Honolulu
